elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, etc.)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.57895/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI present and properly formatted for FAIRhub repository

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI); description: >400 chars explaining multimodal T2DM dataset with AI/ML design rationale
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear title with full expansion and comprehensive description covering dataset purpose, scope, design principles, and FAIR compliance

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, T2DM, AI-READI, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, multimodal dataset, harmonized data, multi-site study, salutogenesis, FAIR principles, retinal imaging, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable devices, biorepository, biospecimens, triple-balanced sampling, health equity, Bridge2AI, cross-sectional study]
sub_elements.quality_note: 19 highly relevant keywords covering disease domain (T2DM), methods (ML, AI, multimodal), study design (triple-balanced, cross-sectional), data types (retinal imaging, CGM, wearables), and program affiliation (Bridge2AI)

sub_elements.name: Dataset Landing Page or Platform URL
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2
sub_elements.quality_note: Active landing page on FAIRhub platform with dataset access and documentation

sub_elements.name: Associated Project or Program
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Bridge2AI]; funders: NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program; external_resources: https://bridge2ai.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear association with Bridge2AI NIH Common Fund program throughout metadata

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Mechanism Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC 4.0; license_and_use_terms describes public access (CC BY-NC) and controlled access (separate DUA)
sub_elements.quality_note: Two-tier access clearly defined: public dataset under CC BY-NC 4.0, controlled dataset requiring data use agreement

sub_elements.name: Data Use Agreement Required?
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'Controlled access data requires a separate data use agreement with the University of Washington as Licensor'
sub_elements.quality_note: DUA requirements explicitly stated for controlled access dataset containing sensitive identifiers and genetic data

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; distributions describe ZIP archives available at FAIRhub
sub_elements.quality_note: FAIRhub platform URL provided with distribution format details (ZIP archives for public and controlled access)

sub_elements.name: File Formats Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (retinal imaging), CSV (tabular/time-series), mHealth standard (wearable data), XML (ECG); distributions specify media_type: application/zip
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple standardized formats clearly documented with specific use cases: DICOM for imaging, CSV for clinical/sensor data, mHealth for wearables, XML for ECG

sub_elements.name: External Links to Similar or Related Datasets
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [AI-READI Project Website (aireadi.org), Dataset Documentation (docs.aireadi.org), FAIRhub Landing Page, Bridge2AI Program, NIH RePORTER, Data Sharing Info, Zenodo Archive, Protocol Publication (BMJ Open), Nature Metabolism Commentary]
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive external resource list including project documentation, parent program (Bridge2AI), grant database, publication DOIs, and archived materials

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC 4.0; license_and_use_terms: 'Permits others to distribute, remix, adapt, build upon this work non-commercially'
sub_elements.quality_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 clearly stated with explicit description of permitted reuse (distribution, remix, adaptation, derivative works) under non-commercial terms

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (ISO 12052 standard for medical imaging), CSV (RFC 4180 standard), mHealth standard (IEEE/OMG standard), XML (W3C standard)
sub_elements.quality_note: All distribution formats use widely adopted international standards: DICOM for imaging interoperability, CSV for tabular data, mHealth for wearable data, XML for structured ECG data

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies mentions 'Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model' but no formal conforms_to field
sub_elements.quality_note: OMOP CDM mentioned in narrative preprocessing text but not formally declared in a conforms_to or standards field; no schema.org, FHIR, or other ontology references

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Defined for Linking
sub_elements.evidence: No data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files field or explicit documentation of participant IDs, linking keys, or unique identifiers for data integration
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing explicit documentation of participant identifiers, record linkage keys, or cross-domain linking mechanisms needed for integrating multimodal data

sub_elements.name: Documentation of Processing Tools for Reproducibility
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods lists devices: Dexcom G6, Garmin VivoSmart 5, REDCap, Philips Pagewriter TC30, MoCA Duo Application, Optomed Aurora IQ, iCare EIDON, Heidelberg Spectralis/FLIO, Topcon Maestro2/Triton, Zeiss Cirrus 5000
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific device models and data collection software named (REDCap, MoCA Duo) but lacks software version numbers, processing pipeline code repositories, or analysis software documentation for full reproducibility

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review Documented
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: 'Study approved by Institutional Review Board (IRB) of University of Washington (approval number STUDY00016228), with reliance agreements from IRBs of University of Alabama at Birmingham and University of California, San Diego'
sub_elements.quality_note: IRB approval number (STUDY00016228) and multi-site reliance agreements clearly documented with lead institution (UW) and participating site IRBs

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified mentions 'de-identification procedures follow applicable regulations and guidelines' but no specific method named
sub_elements.quality_note: Generic statement about de-identification compliance without naming specific methodology (e.g., HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity, or linkage probability thresholds)

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Removed or Masked
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements and confidential_elements describe what's in controlled access (5-digit zip, sex, race, ethnicity, genetic data, health records) but not explicit list of identifiers removed from public dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Documents sensitive data in controlled tier but does not explicitly enumerate identifiers removed or masked in public dataset (e.g., names, dates, SSNs, MRNs, IP addresses per HIPAA 18 identifiers)

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent: 'Written informed consent provided by all participants prior to study enrollment. Consent process conducted in English... developed with bioethics guidance and reviewed by the Community Advisory Board. Participants may withdraw at any time.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Written consent process clearly documented with language requirements (English), bioethics review, Community Advisory Board oversight, and withdrawal rights

sub_elements.name: Ethical Sourcing Statement Included
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research: 'Bioethics guidance integrated throughout study design. Community Advisory Board of 11 persons with diversity in race and ethnicity contributes to protocol development. Ethical and equitable data collection and management practices implemented across all three data collection sites.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive ethical sourcing documentation including bioethics integration, Community Advisory Board (11 diverse members), and explicit commitment to equitable data practices addressing historically underrepresented populations

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Population Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: instances: 'Individual participants aged 40 and older with and without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM)... triple-balanced by self-reported race/ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White), T2DM severity... biological sex (male, female). Participants must speak, read, and understand English. Exclusion criteria include pregnancy and type 1 diabetes.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed population definition with age inclusion (40+), disease stratification (T2DM severity levels), demographic balancing strategy, language requirements, and explicit exclusion criteria

sub_elements.name: Number of Participants or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: 'Target enrollment is 4,000 people'; subpopulations: each group 'target approximately 1,000 participants (25% of sample)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear target enrollment (4,000 total) with specific subpopulation targets (1,000 per race/ethnicity group, 1,000 per diabetes severity level) for triple-balanced design

sub_elements.name: Modalities or Data Types Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: [Survey/questionnaire (REDCap), Physical measurements, Retinal imaging (7 devices), Visual function testing, Clinical laboratory testing, ECG, Cognitive function (MoCA), Peripheral neuropathy assessment, Continuous glucose monitoring, Physical activity monitoring, Environmental monitoring, Biospecimen collection]
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive multimodal data acquisition spanning 12 distinct modalities: surveys, clinical measurements, multi-device imaging, wearables (CGM, fitness tracker), environmental sensors, biospecimens, cognitive testing, and ECG

sub_elements.name: Conditions or Phenotypes Represented
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: [No diabetes (25%), Pre-diabetes and lifestyle-controlled diabetes (25%), Medication-controlled diabetes (25%), Insulin-controlled diabetes (25%)]; purposes: 'salutogenesis (the pathway from disease to health) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus'
sub_elements.quality_note: Disease phenotypes clearly stratified across diabetes severity spectrum (no diabetes, pre-diabetes, medication-controlled, insulin-controlled) to enable salutogenesis trajectory analysis

sub_elements.name: File Dimensions or Sampling Rates Provided
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: 'Dexcom G6 Continuous Glucose Monitor capturing blood glucose measurements (mg/dL) every 5 minutes for 10 days'; 'Garmin VivoSmart 5 wearable device... for 10 days'; 'environmental sensor... for 10 days'; '12-lead ECG'; 'Blood (53 mL) and urine collected'
sub_elements.quality_note: Sampling rates and dimensions documented for time-series data (CGM: 5-minute intervals, 10-day monitoring periods), ECG leads (12-lead), and biospecimen volumes (53 mL blood)

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No dataset_version or version field at document root; versions only mentioned in narrative text: 'pilot data', 'v1.0.0', 'v2.0.0', 'v3.0.0'
sub_elements.quality_note: Version numbers appear in distribution_dates narrative descriptions but not as formal structured metadata field; missing machine-readable version identifier at dataset level

sub_elements.name: Version History Documented
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_dates: [Pilot data release (May 2024), v1.0.0 release (data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024), v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 releases (with additional participants), Final dataset release (after November 2026 enrollment completion)]
sub_elements.quality_note: Version release timeline documented with dates: pilot (May 2024), v1.0.0 (Nov 2024), planned v2.0.0/v3.0.0, final (post-Nov 2026)

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions for Each Version
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_dates mention 'additional participants' as change driver but no detailed changelog, specific participant counts per version, or granular data element additions/modifications
sub_elements.quality_note: Generic description of incremental participant additions across versions but missing detailed changelogs (e.g., 'v1.0.0 added 500 participants, new retinal imaging modality, revised consent form')

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates: 'Dataset updated periodically as enrollment progresses toward target of 4,000 participants by November 2026... Pilot data released May 2024. Data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024 as v1.0.0. Subsequent versions v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 released with additional participants.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Update schedule clearly tied to enrollment milestones with defined endpoint (November 2026 target completion) and periodic release pattern established

sub_elements.name: Versioned Documentation or External References
sub_elements.evidence: version_access: 'All prior versions of the dataset are maintained with version-specific documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org/. Each version includes a changelog and data dictionary. Dataset versioning uses semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0).'
sub_elements.quality_note: Version-specific documentation portal (docs.aireadi.org) with changelogs and data dictionaries for each version; semantic versioning convention (semver) adopted

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Rationale for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: [Understanding T2DM salutogenesis: 'Better understand salutogenesis (the pathway from disease to health) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus using a hypothesis-agnostic, harmonized, multi-domain dataset designed specifically for AI/ML research'; Establishing AI/ML data standards; Addressing demographic inequities in T2DM research]
sub_elements.quality_note: Three-part scientific rationale clearly articulated: (1) salutogenesis research gap, (2) AI-ready data standards establishment, (3) demographic equity in T2DM research

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objective or Task
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: [Enable multi-domain AI/ML analyses for T2DM, Develop unbiased AI/ML models, Study T2DM disease trajectories]; addressing_gaps: 'Provide a large-scale, harmonized, multi-site, multi-domain dataset enabling AI/ML analyses not feasible with existing sources (e.g., claims or EHR alone)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific AI/ML research objectives defined: multi-domain analysis, unbiased model development, disease trajectory/salutogenesis pathway analysis via pseudotime manifold approaches

sub_elements.name: Funding Source or Grant Agency Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program... administered by NIH Office of the Director. Additional support from grants P30DK035816 (Nutrition and Obesity Research Center), UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Primary funding agency (NIH Common Fund) and program (Bridge2AI) clearly identified with supplemental support sources (NORC grant, CTSA grant, Research to Prevent Blindness)

sub_elements.name: Award Number or Grant ID Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders: 'National Institutes of Health grant OT2OD032644... Additional support from grants P30DK035816 (Nutrition and Obesity Research Center), UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness. Total funding in 2022: $5,026,499. Opportunity Number: OTA-21-008. Project dates: September 1, 2022 to August 31, 2025.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Primary grant (OT2OD032644), supplemental grants (P30DK035816, UL1TR003096), opportunity number (OTA-21-008), funding amount ($5,026,499 in 2022), and project period documented

sub_elements.name: Acknowledgement of Platform or Participant Support
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research: 'Community Advisory Board of 11 persons with diversity in race and ethnicity contributes to protocol development'; at_risk_populations: 'A Community Advisory Board of 11 persons with diversity in race and ethnicity provides oversight'
sub_elements.quality_note: Community Advisory Board (11 diverse members) acknowledged for protocol development and oversight; implicit participant acknowledgment through ethical sourcing statements

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Setting or Sites Described
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: 'Single study encounter per participant at one of three data collection sites (Birmingham, San Diego, Seattle)'; data_collectors: 'Trained and certified study coordinators at three data collection sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, University of Washington)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Three collection sites explicitly named with institutional affiliations: UAB (Birmingham, Alabama), UCSD (San Diego, California), UW (Seattle, Washington)

sub_elements.name: Data Capture Method or Device Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods detail 12 modalities with specific devices: REDCap (surveys), Dexcom G6 (CGM), Garmin VivoSmart 5 (activity), Philips Pagewriter TC30 (ECG), MoCA Duo Application (cognitive), Optomed Aurora IQ, iCare EIDON, Heidelberg Spectralis HRA OCT/OCTA/FLIO, Topcon Maestro2 3D OCT-1/Triton DRI OCT, Zeiss Cirrus 5000 (imaging), Topcon KR 800 (autorefraction), M&S Technology EVA tester (visual acuity), Mars Perceptrix chart (contrast sensitivity), custom UW environmental sensor
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive device documentation across all modalities with manufacturer and model: 7 retinal imaging devices, CGM/wearables (Dexcom, Garmin), ECG (Philips), cognitive testing (MoCA Duo), environmental sensors (custom UW design), visual function devices

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing or Cleaning Steps Documented
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: [Data standardization and harmonization across three sites using standardized SOPs and REDCap; Image format conversion from proprietary (.fda, .sdt) to DICOM; Wearable data conversion from .FIT to mHealth standard; Biospecimen processing with standardized local protocols and centralized PBMC isolation; Quality control with standardized training, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements, REDCap validation; Data mapping to standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM)]
sub_elements.quality_note: Five-category preprocessing pipeline documented: multi-site harmonization (SOPs, REDCap), format conversions (proprietary→DICOM, .FIT→mHealth), biospecimen processing standardization, QC procedures, and standards mapping (OMOP, DICOM)

sub_elements.name: Open-Source Processing Code Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No software_and_tools.preprocessing_code field, no GitHub repositories, no code availability statements for format conversion pipelines, DICOM conversion scripts, or mHealth transformation code
sub_elements.quality_note: Processing steps described but no code repositories, scripts, or software packages provided for reproducing format conversions, harmonization procedures, or QC validation pipelines

sub_elements.name: External Standards or References Cited
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [Protocol Publication (BMJ Open): 'BMJ Open publication describing study design and protocol (Owsley et al. 2025) at https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449', Nature Metabolism Commentary: 'Overview of AI-READI approach and significance published in Nature Metabolism at https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x']
sub_elements.quality_note: Peer-reviewed protocol publication (BMJ Open, Owsley et al. 2025, DOI: 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) and methodology commentary (Nature Metabolism, DOI: 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x) referenced

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Limitations Section Present
sub_elements.evidence: No dedicated limitations field at dataset root; limitations discussed within other fields (sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, discouraged_uses)
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations scattered across other sections rather than consolidated in explicit limitations field; missing structured limitations enumeration

sub_elements.name: Sampling Bias or Representativeness Noted
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies.why_not_representative: 'The triple-balanced design intentionally over-samples racial/ethnic minority groups and specific diabetes severity groups relative to their population prevalence, to enable unbiased AI/ML model development. Participants are volunteers, introducing volunteer selection bias that may limit generalizability to non-volunteer populations.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Two key biases explicitly acknowledged: (1) intentional demographic over-sampling relative to population prevalence (triple-balanced design), (2) volunteer selection bias limiting generalizability

sub_elements.name: Quality Control or Validation Steps Mentioned
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: 'Multiple quality control measures including standardized training of study coordinators, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements, and data validation checks in REDCap system. Data managers at each site oversee quality control before uploading to FAIRhub.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Multi-level QC documented: coordinator certification, equipment calibration, measurement duplication for reliability, REDCap validation rules, site data manager oversight before release

sub_elements.name: Known Risks or Use Constraints Listed
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses: [Uses during ongoing enrollment without awareness of limitations (balanced distribution not yet achieved), Clinical decision-making without validation, Re-identification attempts]; prohibited_uses: [Clinical treatment decisions, Re-identification of participants, Sharing with non-licensed parties]
sub_elements.quality_note: Three discouraged uses (incomplete enrollment awareness, unvalidated clinical use, re-identification) and three prohibited uses (clinical treatment, re-identification, unauthorized sharing) clearly enumerated

sub_elements.name: Conflicts of Interest Declared
sub_elements.evidence: No ethics.conflicts_of_interest field or COI statement for dataset creators, funders, or institutional affiliations
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing conflicts of interest disclosure for principal investigators, co-investigators, institutional partners, or funding relationships beyond grant acknowledgments

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; distributions: 'Public access subset... available at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2'; external_resources: 'FAIRhub Dataset Landing Page... at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2'
sub_elements.quality_note: Published on FAIRhub (fairhub.io), a recognized FAIR-compliant biomedical data repository platform with DOI minting and access control capabilities

sub_elements.name: Cross-referenced DOIs or Related Dataset Links
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [Zenodo Archive (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10642459), Protocol Publication BMJ Open (https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), Nature Metabolism Commentary (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), NIH RePORTER Project Details (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10471118)]
sub_elements.quality_note: Three publication DOIs (Zenodo dataset DOI, BMJ Open protocol DOI, Nature Metabolism commentary DOI) plus NIH RePORTER grant record cross-referenced

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Reference
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: 'All data mapped to applicable data standard formats such as Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM format for retinal imaging'; distribution_formats: DICOM (ISO 12052), mHealth standard (IEEE/OMG)
sub_elements.quality_note: Three community standards referenced: OMOP CDM for clinical data interoperability, DICOM (ISO 12052) for imaging, mHealth (IEEE/OMG) for wearable data; however, no schema.org or formal conforms_to field

sub_elements.name: Associated Outreach Materials
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: [AI-READI Project Website (https://aireadi.org/), AI-READI Dataset Documentation (https://docs.aireadi.org/ with version-specific guides), Data Sharing Information (https://aireadi.org/goals/data-sharing)]
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive documentation ecosystem: project website (aireadi.org), versioned user guides (docs.aireadi.org), data sharing policies; missing tutorials/webinars but strong documentation presence

sub_elements.name: Similar Dataset Links or Thematic Grouping
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Bridge2AI Program (https://bridge2ai.org/); keywords: [Bridge2AI]; funders: 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear thematic grouping within Bridge2AI NIH Common Fund consortium of AI-ready biomedical datasets; Bridge2AI program portal links to related datasets (VOICE, CM4AI, CHORUS)

strengths: Comprehensive discovery metadata with DOI (10.57895/fairhub.2), 19 relevant keywords, and clear Bridge2AI program affiliation enabling findability
Two-tier access model (CC BY-NC 4.0 public, DUA-controlled sensitive) with explicit FAIRhub distribution platform and standardized formats (DICOM, CSV, mHealth, XML)

Detailed composition documentation: 4,000-participant target, triple-balanced design (race/ethnicity × sex × diabetes severity), 12 multimodal data domains with specific sampling rates (CGM: 5-min intervals)
Strong ethical documentation: IRB approval (STUDY00016228) with multi-site reliance agreements, written informed consent, Community Advisory Board (11 diverse members) oversight
Transparent scientific motivation with three-part rationale (salutogenesis research, AI/ML standards, health equity) backed by full funding details (NIH OT2OD032644, $5M, 2022-2025)
Comprehensive technical transparency: three named sites (UAB/UCSD/UW), 20+ specific devices documented (7 retinal imaging systems, Dexcom G6, Garmin VivoSmart 5), five-category preprocessing pipeline
Cross-platform integration via FAIRhub with three publication DOIs (Zenodo, BMJ Open protocol, Nature Metabolism commentary) and Bridge2AI thematic consortium linkage
weaknesses: Missing formal conforms_to field declaring schema/ontology conformance; OMOP CDM mentioned in preprocessing narrative but not machine-readable standards declaration
No documentation of participant identifiers or linking keys (data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files) needed for cross-domain data integration in multimodal dataset
Device models documented but missing software version numbers, processing code repositories (GitHub), or analysis pipeline scripts for full computational reproducibility
De-identification approach not specified (no HIPAA Safe Harbor vs Expert Determination vs k-anonymity method declaration); identifiers removed from public dataset not enumerated
No formal dataset_version field at document root; version numbers (v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0) only in narrative text; missing detailed version changelogs beyond 'additional participants'
No dedicated limitations section consolidating known constraints; limitations scattered across sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and discouraged_uses fields
No conflicts of interest disclosure for principal investigators, co-investigators, or institutional partners beyond grant funding acknowledgments
Missing open-source preprocessing code for format conversions (proprietary→DICOM, .FIT→mHealth), harmonization pipelines, or QC validation procedures
recommendations: Add conforms_to field declaring OMOP CDM conformance for clinical data, DICOM for imaging, mHealth for wearables to enable automated schema validation and interoperability discovery
Document participant identifiers and cross-domain linking mechanisms in data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files (e.g., participant_id structure, visit codes, sample IDs for biospecimen linkage)
Create software_and_tools.preprocessing_code section with GitHub repositories for DICOM conversion scripts, .FIT→mHealth transformation code, and multi-site harmonization pipelines
Add deidentification_and_privacy.approach field specifying HIPAA Safe Harbor compliance and deidentification_and_privacy.examples_of_identifiers_removed with 18 HIPAA identifiers checklist

Promote dataset_version to top-level field (e.g., dataset_version: 1.0.0) with machine-readable semantic versioning; expand distribution_dates change descriptions with participant counts and modality additions per version

Consolidate limitations into dedicated limitations section enumerating: (1) triple-balanced over-sampling bias, (2) volunteer selection bias, (3) ongoing enrollment incompleteness, (4) English-language requirement, (5) cross-sectional design (no longitudinal follow-up)
Add ethics.conflicts_of_interest field with COI statements for 20 named creators/co-investigators and institutional relationships (especially industry device partnerships for imaging equipment)

Publish preprocessing pipelines to GitHub with DOI-versioned releases on Zenodo; document software versions (REDCap version, imaging device firmware, Dexcom/Garmin SDK versions) in preprocessing_strategies

Add data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files documenting participant_id format, record linking keys, and cross-modality join mechanisms (e.g., 'participant_id links survey→clinical→imaging→wearable data; biospecimen_id links samples→lab results')
